plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 3-era timeline completes: Oct 1667 & 1904 (Robert Hooke & Richard Lower prove venous blood turns scarlet by absorbing air in the lungs; Christian Bohr discovers the sigmoidal haemoglobin O2 curve and the Bohr Effect) · 1910 (August Krogh & Marie Krogh publish 'The Seven Little Devils' microtonometer proof that oxygen crosses the 300 million alveoli by 100% passive diffusion, winning the 1920 Nobel Prize) · May 1959 & 13 Feb 1960 (Kurt von Neergaard 1929, John Clements 1957 & Mary Ellen Avery May 1959 discover pulmonary surfactant and the cause of newborn respiratory distress; Max Perutz solves the 3D X-ray structure of haemoglobin, winning the 1962 Nobel Prize).

teach_overlay.scale: from fireplace bellows in seventeenth-century London to a microscopic gas bubble in Copenhagen, an X-ray beam in Cambridge, and a soap trough in Boston, scientists unlocked the tennis-court sponge that keeps us breathing
